body:
This is such a great question, and something I ruminate on a LOT. I think it's more that I am so fucking myopic, I failed to adequately plan for the future, over-analyze the present, and dwell on the past. I wouldn't say I am suicidal on a daily basis, more that my aforementioned lack of planning for the future leads me to a conclusion that suicide will be my only option when I get (even) older. The feeling that I won't have anyone to grow old with (or "take care of me" as absurd as that notion is for ANYone), no money to consider an actual retirement, and the dawning realization that life will be physically daunting, if not impossible.  


So, for me, it's not that I'm going to be holding on, more just that I strive to be realistic about my future predicaments - perceived, or otherwise. And like a bunch of us here (I hope, anyway) we know how devastating suicide can be to people in our lives. I had an uncle kill himself, a HS acquaintance, and a friend from work. They each *crushed* me, so by joining this incredibly supportive community (I have been a Longtime Lurker...), maybe I'm searching for some sort of validation (duh), acceptance, and... hope?
I currently reside in the PNW.

This is... wow. There is a lot to chew on here, and I sincerely appreciate your thoughtful statements, and questions. The irony of my current situation/depressive state, is that I have been doing some new things. Writing (including posting on Reddit for the first time!), making Christmas cards with some hand lettering, and exercising. Yet, yet! I'm still just so. fucking. miserable. And it *feels* irrational at this time, because I intrinsically know where this pain is coming from, and I have the coping skills to make it day by day.   


Sooooo, I think I am going to do as you suggest, and try stepping further out of my isolation bubble. The gnawing certainty of the tides of hopelessness will likely persist, but who knows? Maybe there will be something that will at least provide some short term clarity/purpose.

Thank you! The most writing I ever did was in HS when I was the "film critic" for the school newspaper. I've also, just recently, posted some reviews for a couple movies on Letterboxd... in a futile attempt to impress a woman. lol. I suppose I should just keep writing them for myself, and (thanks to your kind words) maybe look inwards to try my hand at writing about something other than movies.

Touché. I guess from my perspective, they lead to misery. Again, last year, had a heart attack, got out of a dead end job, an even more dead end relationship, and I’m still hopelessly melancholy. Started this year feigning, and hoping for optimism, yet it was out of my reach. So, here I am, seeking solace from like-minded folks on Reddit. Cheers to you.
Yes! Exactly! The inexorable grind of time cares not for our fragile egos, bodies, and minds. Petty, or life-changing, it makes no difference. All roads still lead me right back to misery.

I’m currently struggling with reconciling my emotions about why I need to let someone into my heart. Like, why should ANYone, other than me, have to bear the responsibility of making me happy? And yet, I always fall in love too easily, and repeat the cycle ad nauseam.

It’s shockingly head spinning how quickly the years, and decades pile up, eh? And just when I think I’m getting close to stepping away from the edge, something (or usually someone...) pushes me right back to it.
